Genesis.name: Genesis
Genesis.author: Moses
Genesis.theme: Origins, Creation, Fall, and Covenant Promises
Genesis.key_verse: Genesis 1:1 - In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
Genesis.description: Genesis is the foundational narrative of creation, human identity, and the tragic fall into sin. Out of the darkness, God calls Abraham into a sacred covenant to bless all the nations of the earth.
Genesis.review: Genesis demonstrates the unwavering faithfulness of God in fulfilling His promises across generations. What human malice designed for harm, divine providence transforms into redemption and enduring life.

Exodus.name: Exodus
Exodus.author: Moses
Exodus.theme: Deliverance, Passover, the Law, and the Tabernacle
Exodus.key_verse: Exodus 3:14 - And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM.
Exodus.description: Exodus showcases the mighty power of God breaking the chains of Egyptian bondage to liberate His people. At Mount Sinai, God delivers His holy commandments and establishes a sacred sanctuary to dwell among them.
Exodus.review: Exodus culminates in the radiant glory of the Lord descending upon the Tabernacle. Deliverance is revealed not merely as freedom from oppression, but as intimate fellowship with the living God.

Leviticus.name: Leviticus
Leviticus.author: Moses
Leviticus.theme: Holiness, Sacrificial Atonement, and True Worship
Leviticus.key_verse: Leviticus 19:2 - Ye shall be holy: for I the LORD your God am holy.
Leviticus.description: Leviticus provides the sacred instructions for ritual purity, priesthood, and atoning sacrifices. It establishes the principle that a holy God desires to abide with an imperfect people through gracious atonement.
Leviticus.review: Leviticus reveals the immense weight of holiness and the beauty of forgiveness. The sacrificial system foreshadows the supreme offering of Christ, who cleanses conscience and opens the way to God.

Numbers.name: Numbers
Numbers.author: Moses
Numbers.theme: Wilderness Journey, Divine Discipline, and Faithfulness
Numbers.key_verse: Numbers 6:24-26 - The LORD bless thee, and keep thee: The LORD make his face shine upon thee.
Numbers.description: Numbers chronicles the wilderness wanderings of Israel from Sinai toward the border of Canaan. It records both the sorrowful cost of human unbelief and the steadfast provision of God who never abandons His oath.
Numbers.review: Numbers reminds us that even when our footsteps falter in dry desert seasons, God remains faithful. His divine guidance by cloud and fire leads every humble heart safely to the promised rest.

Deuteronomy.name: Deuteronomy
Deuteronomy.author: Moses
Deuteronomy.theme: Covenant Renewal, Wholehearted Devotion, and Obedience
Deuteronomy.key_verse: Deuteronomy 6:5 - And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul.
Deuteronomy.description: Deuteronomy gathers the heartfelt farewell messages of Moses delivered upon the plains of Moab. He urges the new generation to remember their history, keep the commandments, and love God with all their being.
Deuteronomy.review: Deuteronomy stands as an enduring call to passionate, heartfelt obedience. God seeks not outward rituals, but genuine love and righteous justice lived out in every sphere of human existence.

Joshua.name: Joshua
Joshua.author: Joshua / Early Chronicler
Joshua.theme: Conquest, Courage, and Claiming the Divine Inheritance
Joshua.key_verse: Joshua 1:9 - Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed.
Joshua.description: Joshua records the triumph of faith as Israel crosses the Jordan and claims the promised land. Fortress walls fall and waters part as the Lord Himself fights for those who walk in courageous trust.
Joshua.review: Joshua proves that every promise of God holds true; not one word has ever failed. Victory and peace are granted to those who consecrate their hearts and choose to serve the Lord faithfully.

Judges.name: Judges
Judges.author: Traditionally Samuel
Judges.theme: Cycles of Apostasy, Deliverance, and the Need for a King
Judges.key_verse: Judges 21:25 - In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.
Judges.description: Judges depicts a dark era marked by repeated cycles of rebellion, oppression, cry for mercy, and divine rescue. God repeatedly raises up courageous leaders like Deborah and Gideon to deliver His people.
Judges.review: Judges warns against moral compromise while highlighting God unbounded mercy. In our deepest weakness and failure, the Lord hears the cry of repentance and provides salvation.

Ruth.name: Ruth
Ruth.author: Traditionally Samuel
Ruth.key_verse: Ruth 1:16 - Intreat me not to leave thee: for whither thou goest, I will go.
Ruth.description: Ruth is a radiant story of loyalty and providence set against the dark days of the judges. A devoted foreign widow chooses faith in the God of Israel and discovers generous redemption through Boaz.
Ruth.review: Ruth shows how quiet acts of kindness and steadfast faith are woven into the grand tapestry of redemption. Through this humble family line came King David and ultimately the Messiah.

1 Samuel.name: 1 Samuel
1 Samuel.author: Samuel, Nathan, and Gad
1 Samuel.theme: The Rise of the Monarchy; Looking at the Heart
1 Samuel.key_verse: 1 Samuel 16:7 - For man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart.
1 Samuel.description: 1 Samuel traces the transition from judges to kings through Samuel the prophet, Saul the tragic first monarch, and David the courageous shepherd boy who defeated the giant Goliath in the name of the Lord.
1 Samuel.review: 1 Samuel demonstrates that outward position cannot substitute for inner integrity. Saul lost his crown through pride, while David was exalted because his heart was yielded to God.

2 Samuel.name: 2 Samuel
2 Samuel.author: Nathan and Gad
2 Samuel.theme: David Reign, the Eternal Covenant, and Repentance
2 Samuel.key_verse: 2 Samuel 7:16 - And thine house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee.
2 Samuel.description: 2 Samuel chronicles the united reign of King David, the establishment of Jerusalem, and God eternal covenant promise to establish his royal lineage through an everlasting kingdom.
2 Samuel.review: 2 Samuel balances glorious triumphs with the sobering consequences of moral failure. Yet David humble confession and restored communion testify to the unfailing mercy of the Almighty.

1 Kings.name: 1 Kings
1 Kings.author: Jeremiah / Biblical Author
1 Kings.theme: Solomon Wisdom, the Splendid Temple, and Division
1 Kings.key_verse: 1 Kings 3:9 - Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people.
1 Kings.description: 1 Kings opens with the splendor of Solomon temple and the zenith of Israelite wealth, but concludes with idolatry, tragic national division into northern and southern kingdoms, and the bold ministry of Elijah.
1 Kings.review: 1 Kings reveals that worldly wisdom and prosperity cannot safeguard a divided heart. Faithfulness to God commandments is the only true foundation for lasting peace and national well-being.

2 Kings.name: 2 Kings
2 Kings.author: Jeremiah / Biblical Author
2 Kings.theme: Decline, Prophetic Warnings, and the Babylonian Exile
2 Kings.key_verse: 2 Kings 17:13 - Turn ye from your evil ways, and keep my commandments and my statutes.
2 Kings.description: 2 Kings traces the decline and fall of both divided kingdoms despite the fiery ministries of Elisha and righteous reforms of Hezekiah and Josiah. Unfaithfulness ultimately results in tragic exile.
2 Kings.review: 2 Kings confirms that God patience is immense, yet His moral universe demands justice. Even in the ashes of Jerusalem, the preservation of the royal line keeps hope alive for future restoration.

1 Chronicles.name: 1 Chronicles
1 Chronicles.author: Traditionally Ezra
1 Chronicles.theme: Genealogies, Temple Worship, and David Legacy
1 Chronicles.key_verse: 1 Chronicles 16:34 - O give thanks unto the LORD; for he is good; for his mercy endureth for ever.
1 Chronicles.description: 1 Chronicles retells the sacred history for returning exiles, spotlighting David devotion to worship, the organization of musicians and priests, and extensive preparations to build the holy temple.
1 Chronicles.review: 1 Chronicles reminds a restored community of their eternal spiritual identity. True greatness is measured by placing worship and thanksgiving at the center of personal and national life.

2 Chronicles.name: 2 Chronicles
2 Chronicles.author: Traditionally Ezra
2 Chronicles.theme: The Glory of the Temple, Kings, and National Revival
2 Chronicles.key_verse: 2 Chronicles 7:14 - If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, then will I hear from heaven.
2 Chronicles.description: 2 Chronicles highlights the spiritual revivals under Judah faithful kings and the magnificent dedication of Solomon temple, concluding with the decree of King Cyrus granting permission to rebuild.
2 Chronicles.review: 2 Chronicles emphasizes that whenever God people humble themselves, seek His face, and turn from wrongdoing, divine healing and spiritual restoration are poured out abundantly.

Ezra.name: Ezra
Ezra.author: Ezra
Ezra.theme: Return from Exile, Rebuilding the Temple, and Scripture
Ezra.key_verse: Ezra 7:10 - For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the LORD, and to do it.
Ezra.description: Ezra records the joyous return of Jewish exiles to their homeland, the miraculous reconstruction of the temple amidst fierce opposition, and a profound revival centered on the study of the Scriptures.
Ezra.review: Ezra demonstrates that renewal begins in personal commitment to study, live, and teach God truth. Faithfulness and prayer conquer all political obstacles and renew broken communities.

Nehemiah.name: Nehemiah
Nehemiah.author: Nehemiah
Nehemiah.theme: Rebuilding the Walls, Courageous Leadership, and Reform
Nehemiah.key_verse: Nehemiah 8:10 - The joy of the LORD is your strength.
Nehemiah.description: Nehemiah tells the inspiring account of a royal cupbearer who leads the rebuilding of Jerusalem defensive walls in fifty-two days despite threats, slander, and immense social injustice.
Nehemiah.review: Nehemiah shows that prayer combined with diligent labor and righteous leadership achieves the impossible. The joy of the Lord strengthens us to rebuild what lies in ruins.

Esther.name: Esther
Esther.author: Unknown Jewish Scribe
Esther.theme: Providence, Courage, and Deliverance in the Persian Court
Esther.key_verse: Esther 4:14 - And who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
Esther.description: Esther portrays a young Jewish orphan who becomes queen of Persia and risks her life to thwart an empire-wide plot of genocide. God invisible hand orchestrates every circumstance for deliverance.
Esther.review: Esther proves that even when God name is not overtly spoken, His sovereign providence directs history. Courageous faith steps up for such a time as this to defend truth and righteousness.

Job.name: Job
Job.author: Unknown Scribe / Job
Job.theme: Suffering, Sovereignty, and Unshakeable Faith in God
Job.key_verse: Job 19:25 - For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth.
Job.description: Job wrestles with the profound mystery of innocent suffering through poetic dialogues between Job and his companions, leading to a majestic encounter with the Creator from the midst of the whirlwind.
Job.review: Job reveals that true faith trusts God character even in the absence of easy answers. In the end, God majesty comforts the sorrowing and restores hope far beyond our comprehension.

Psalms.name: Psalms
Psalms.author: David, Asaph, Sons of Korah, and others
Psalms.theme: Praise, Lament, Thanksgiving, and Prayer in All Seasons
Psalms.key_verse: Psalms 23:1 - The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
Psalms.description: Psalms is the timeless prayerbook and hymnal of God people. It spans the full range of human emotion—from despair and sorrow to soaring praise, exalting God mercy, power, and everlasting love.
Psalms.review: Psalms teaches us to pour out our entire hearts before God in complete honesty. Whatever storm surrounds us, praise reorients the soul toward divine sovereignty and steadfast peace.

Proverbs.name: Proverbs
Proverbs.author: Solomon, Agur, and Lemuel
Proverbs.theme: Practical Wisdom, the Fear of the Lord, and Righteous Living
Proverbs.key_verse: Proverbs 3:5-6 - Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
Proverbs.description: Proverbs distills practical divine wisdom for everyday life into memorable maxims. It guides decisions regarding speech, integrity, finances, friendship, and family, rooted in reverence for the Lord.
Proverbs.review: Proverbs demonstrates that godly wisdom is a tree of life. Choosing the path of humility, discipline, and understanding yields peace, protection, and fruitful honor.

Ecclesiastes.name: Ecclesiastes
Ecclesiastes.author: Solomon (The Preacher)
Ecclesiastes.theme: The Meaning of Life, Vanity under the Sun, and Eternity
Ecclesiastes.key_verse: Ecclesiastes 12:13 - Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.
Ecclesiastes.description: Ecclesiastes investigates the meaning of existence from an earthly perspective, declaring earthly pursuits of pleasure, wealth, and status to be fleeting vapor apart from the eternal Creator.
Ecclesiastes.review: Ecclesiastes strips away empty illusions to uncover what truly matters. Life finds genuine joy, purpose, and contentment only when centered on revering God and honoring His commandments.

Song of Solomon.name: Song of Solomon
Song of Solomon.author: Solomon
Song of Solomon.theme: Marital Love, Pure Passion, and Covenant Delight
Song of Solomon.key_verse: Song of Solomon 8:6-7 - Love is strong as death... Many waters cannot quench love.
Song of Solomon.description: Song of Solomon is an exquisite poetic celebration of romantic affection, marital intimacy, and reciprocal commitment between a bride and her groom in divine beauty and purity.
Song of Solomon.review: Song of Solomon honors marital devotion as a holy gift from God, reflecting the profound love, relentless pursuit, and eternal fidelity between the divine Bridegroom and His people.

Isaiah.name: Isaiah
Isaiah.author: Isaiah son of Amoz
Isaiah.theme: The Holy One of Israel, Judgment, and the Suffering Servant
Isaiah.key_verse: Isaiah 9:6 - For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counseller.
Isaiah.description: Isaiah is often hailed as the fifth Gospel for its sweeping visions of the Holy One of Israel, majestic prophecies of the virgin-born Emmanuel, and the poignant portrait of the Suffering Servant.
Isaiah.review: Isaiah anchors our confidence in the ultimate triumph of God righteous kingdom. Through the wounds of the Redeemer, healing and redemption are offered to every longing heart.

Jeremiah.name: Jeremiah
Jeremiah.author: Jeremiah
Jeremiah.theme: Prophetic Warning, the Weeping Prophet, and the New Covenant
Jeremiah.key_verse: Jeremiah 29:11 - For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil.
Jeremiah.description: Jeremiah faithfully proclaims truth to an obstinate nation for four decades amidst personal persecution and heartbreak. He foretells the coming exile alongside the dawn of an internal New Covenant.
Jeremiah.review: Jeremiah models steadfast perseverance in the face of spiritual apathy. Even in desolation, God writes His law upon the human heart and promises an unshakeable future filled with hope.

Lamentations.name: Lamentations
Lamentations.author: Jeremiah
Lamentations.theme: Sorrow over Jerusalem Fall and Unfailing Compassions
Lamentations.key_verse: Lamentations 3:22-23 - It is of the LORD mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning.
Lamentations.description: Lamentations consists of five poignant acrostic dirges mourning the burning of Jerusalem and the destruction of the holy temple, expressing profound grief with unvarnished honesty.
Lamentations.review: Lamentations stands as an anthem of hope in the deepest night of tragedy. Even amid grief, the steadfast mercies of the Lord are renewed every single morning; great is His faithfulness.

Ezekiel.name: Ezekiel
Ezekiel.author: Ezekiel the Priest
Ezekiel.theme: The Glory of God, Valley of Dry Bones, and Temple Restored
Ezekiel.key_verse: Ezekiel 36:26 - A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you.
Ezekiel.description: Ezekiel ministers to exiles in Babylon through vivid symbolic street theater and dazzling apocalyptic visions of heavenly chariots, reviving dry bones into a living army, and a glorious river of life.
Ezekiel.review: Ezekiel guarantees that spiritual renewal comes through the Holy Spirit breathing life into dead places. God gives a new heart of flesh and restores divine presence forever.

Daniel.name: Daniel
Daniel.author: Daniel
Daniel.theme: Faith in Babylon, the Fiery Furnace, and Sovereign Kingdoms
Daniel.key_verse: Daniel 2:44 - And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed.
Daniel.description: Daniel chronicles courageous young men who refused to defile themselves in pagan Babylon. Through miraculous deliverance from blazing furnaces and lions, God reveals His reign over all world empires.
Daniel.review: Daniel declares that human empires rise and fall according to divine appointment, but the kingdom of God shall stand indestructible forever. Courageous integrity honors God in every culture.

Hosea.name: Hosea
Hosea.author: Hosea son of Beeri
Hosea.theme: Relentless Love, Spiritual Adultery, and Gracious Healing
Hosea.key_verse: Hosea 6:6 - For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
Hosea.description: Hosea portrays the heartbreak of divine love through the prophet marriage to an unfaithful spouse, dramatizing God fierce, enduring commitment to redeem His wayward bride.
Hosea.review: Hosea magnifies the astonishing grace that pursues us into our brokenness. God love refuses to let go, offering healing, forgiveness, and renewal to all who return.

Joel.name: Joel
Joel.author: Joel son of Pethuel
Joel.theme: The Locust Plague, the Day of the Lord, and the Outpouring of the Spirit
Joel.key_verse: Joel 2:28 - And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh.
Joel.description: Joel interprets a catastrophic locust invasion as a harbinger of the great Day of the Lord, calling the nation to rend their hearts and promising a universal outpouring of the Holy Spirit.
Joel.review: Joel reminds us that true repentance brings restoration of years the locusts have eaten. Whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved and filled with divine power.

Amos.name: Amos
Amos.author: Amos of Tekoa
Amos.theme: Social Justice, Righteousness like a River, and Divine Standard
Amos.key_verse: Amos 5:24 - But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.
Amos.description: Amos, a humble shepherd and fig grower, boldly confronts the affluent northern kingdom for exploiting the poor, upholding religious hypocrisy, and silencing moral conviction.
Amos.review: Amos thunders against empty religiosity detached from love for neighbors. True worship overflows in defending the vulnerable and establishing justice like an unfailing stream.

Obadiah.name: Obadiah
Obadiah.author: Obadiah
Obadiah.theme: Pride of Edom, Brotherly Treachery, and God Kingdom Exalted
Obadiah.key_verse: Obadiah 1:21 - And saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the LORD.
Obadiah.description: Obadiah delivers a sharp oracle against Edom for rejoicing in Jerusalem downfall and exploiting their brethren in distress. It proclaims the downfall of pride and victory of Mount Zion.
Obadiah.review: Obadiah demonstrates that self-sufficient arrogance and cruelty toward others lead to ruin. The sovereign Lord defends His afflicted children and establishes His righteous reign.

Jonah.name: Jonah
Jonah.author: Jonah son of Amittai
Jonah.theme: The Reluctant Prophet, the Great Fish, and Mercy for Nineveh
Jonah.key_verse: Jonah 2:9 - Salvation is of the LORD.
Jonah.description: Jonah flees from his calling to preach in Nineveh, survives three days in the belly of a great fish, and witnesses the astonishing repentance of an entire pagan metropolis.
Jonah.review: Jonah reveals that God compassions are boundless, reaching beyond all national and cultural borders. Salvation belongs entirely to the Lord, who delights in showing mercy.

Micah.name: Micah
Micah.author: Micah of Moresheth
Micah.theme: Justice, Mercy, Walking Humbly, and the Bethlehem Ruler
Micah.key_verse: Micah 6:8 - What doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?
Micah.description: Micah balances piercing indictments of corrupt leaders with luminous visions of mountain peace, prophesying that the eternal Ruler will be born in the humble village of Bethlehem.
Micah.review: Micah summarizes true religion in doing justice, loving mercy, and walking humbly with God. Our Lord pardons iniquity and casts our sins into the depths of the sea.

Nahum.name: Nahum
Nahum.author: Nahum of Elkosh
Nahum.theme: The Fall of Nineveh and God Protection of the Oppressed
Nahum.key_verse: Nahum 1:7 - The LORD is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that trust in him.
Nahum.description: Nahum pronounces the righteous judgment awaiting the bloodthirsty Assyrian empire, celebrating the liberation of oppressed captives and comforting those who take refuge in God.
Nahum.review: Nahum affirms that tyranny and cruelty have an expiration date. The Lord is slow to anger but great in power, standing as a faithful fortress in the day of trouble.

Habakkuk.name: Habakkuk
Habakkuk.author: Habakkuk
Habakkuk.theme: Questioning Injustice, the Just Living by Faith, and Joy in God
Habakkuk.key_verse: Habakkuk 2:4 - But the just shall live by his faith.
Habakkuk.description: Habakkuk dialogues with God concerning rampant injustice and the impending Babylonian invasion, concluding with a magnificent hymn of trust even when all crops fail.
Habakkuk.review: Habakkuk models honest wrestling that resolves in triumphant joy. Even in economic collapse and earthly desolation, the just shall live by faith, rejoicing in the God of their salvation.

Zephaniah.name: Zephaniah
Zephaniah.author: Zephaniah
Zephaniah.theme: The Day of Wrath, Purification, and God Singing over His People
Zephaniah.key_verse: Zephaniah 3:17 - The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy.
Zephaniah.description: Zephaniah heralds global judgment upon corruption while envisioning a purified remnant from all nations gathered in worship, rejoicing as God Himself sings over them in love.
Zephaniah.review: Zephaniah reminds us that purification precedes glorious restoration. God removes shame, gathers the outcast, and rejoices over His redeemed children with songs of joy.

Haggai.name: Haggai
Haggai.author: Haggai
Haggai.theme: Rebuilding God House, Reordered Priorities, and Greater Glory
Haggai.key_verse: Haggai 1:8 - Go up to the mountain, and bring wood, and build the house; and I will take pleasure in it.
Haggai.description: Haggai delivers four urgent messages to returned exiles who neglected the temple to build paneled homes for themselves, inspiring them to resume the work and promise greater future glory.
Haggai.review: Haggai challenges us to align our daily priorities with God eternal kingdom. When we honor Him first, His presence fills our labor with divine peace and spiritual abundance.

Zechariah.name: Zechariah
Zechariah.author: Zechariah son of Berechiah
Zechariah.theme: Night Visions, the Coming King on a Donkey, and Cleansing Fountain
Zechariah.key_verse: Zechariah 4:6 - Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts.
Zechariah.description: Zechariah combines apocalyptic night visions with messianic prophecies, foretelling the King arriving gently upon a colt, pierced for our transgressions, and inaugurating a fountain of cleansing.
Zechariah.review: Zechariah declares that God kingdom advances not through human military prowess, but by the Holy Spirit. A day is coming when the Lord shall be King over all the earth.

Malachi.name: Malachi
Malachi.author: Malachi
Malachi.theme: Covenant Faithfulness, Honest Giving, and the Sun of Righteousness
Malachi.key_verse: Malachi 4:2 - But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings.
Malachi.description: Malachi confronts spiritual lukewarmness, corrupt sacrifices, and broken marriages among returned exiles, pointing forward to Elijah coming and the dawn of the Sun of Righteousness.
Malachi.review: Malachi closes the Old Testament canon with the anticipation of dawn. For those who revere His name, healing and joy arise like the morning sun, breaking centuries of silence.

Matthew.name: Matthew
Matthew.author: Matthew (Levi)
Matthew.theme: Jesus the Promised King of the Jews, the Sermon on the Mount, and Great Commission
Matthew.key_verse: Matthew 28:19-20 - Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them... and, lo, I am with you alway.
Matthew.description: Matthew presents Jesus of Nazareth as the long-awaited Messianic King who fulfills ancient prophecy, delivers the revolutionary Sermon on the Mount, and commissions His disciples to disciple all nations.
Matthew.review: Matthew grounds our faith in the authority and presence of King Jesus. Having conquered sin and the grave, He reigns supreme and promises to accompany His followers always.

Mark.name: Mark
Mark.author: John Mark
Mark.theme: The Suffering Servant, Immediate Action, and the Ransom for Many
Mark.key_verse: Mark 10:45 - For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.
Mark.description: Mark moves with breathless urgency to depict Jesus as the mighty Servant of God, performing compassionate miracles, confronting demonic oppression, and walking resolutely to the cross.
Mark.review: Mark challenges us to take up our cross and follow the humble Servant. True greatness in the kingdom of God is found in sacrificial service and radical love.

Luke.name: Luke
Luke.author: Luke the Physician
Luke.theme: The Son of Man Seeking and Saving the Lost; Compassion for All
Luke.key_verse: Luke 19:10 - For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.
Luke.description: Luke crafts an orderly historical account highlighting Jesus compassion for outcasts, women, the poor, and Samaritans, featuring beloved parables like the Prodigal Son and the Good Samaritan.
Luke.review: Luke reassures us that the love of Christ reaches to the ends of the earth and into the darkest margins. The Good Shepherd never stops searching until every lost child is safely home.

John.name: John
John.author: John the Beloved Apostle
John.theme: The Incarnate Word, Seven Signs, Eternal Life, and Divine Love
John.key_verse: John 3:16 - For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish.
John.description: John presents Jesus as the divine Word made flesh, weaving together seven miraculous signs and majestic I AM statements to lead readers to unshakeable belief and abundant eternal life.
John.review: John invites us into intimate friendship and fellowship with God. In Christ we behold divine glory, receive unmeasured grace, and step out of darkness into everlasting light.

Acts.name: Acts
Acts.author: Luke the Physician
Acts.theme: The Holy Spirit, the Birth of the Church, and Gospel to the Nations
Acts.key_verse: Acts 1:8 - But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me.
Acts.description: Acts chronicles the explosion of the early church from the Upper Room in Jerusalem through Judea, Samaria, and all the way to imperial Rome, driven by the Holy Spirit and fearless witness.
Acts.review: Acts demonstrates that no prison, persecution, or storm can hinder the unstoppable advance of the Gospel. Empowered by the Holy Spirit, everyday believers turn the world upside down.

Romans.name: Romans
Romans.author: Paul the Apostle
Romans.theme: Justification by Faith, Grace, Life in the Spirit, and No Condemnation
Romans.key_verse: Romans 8:28 - And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God.
Romans.description: Romans is Paul masterwork of theological precision, systematically exploring universal human sin, free justification by grace through faith in Christ, and life of radical love.
Romans.review: Romans secures our soul in the unbreakable love of God. There is now no condemnation for those in Christ Jesus, nor any power in heaven or earth that can separate us from His love.

1 Corinthians.name: 1 Corinthians
1 Corinthians.author: Paul the Apostle
1 Corinthians.theme: Unity in the Body, Spiritual Gifts, Christian Love, and the Resurrection
1 Corinthians.key_verse: 1 Corinthians 13:13 - And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.
1 Corinthians.description: 1 Corinthians addresses divisions, moral compromises, and disorderly worship in Corinth, culminating in the immortal ode to self-giving love and the triumphant defense of bodily resurrection.
1 Corinthians.review: 1 Corinthians reminds us that supernatural spiritual gifts mean nothing without selfless love. Death has been swallowed up in victory through our risen Lord Jesus Christ.

2 Corinthians.name: 2 Corinthians
2 Corinthians.author: Paul the Apostle
2 Corinthians.theme: Comfort in Affliction, Strength in Weakness, and Ministry of Reconciliation
2 Corinthians.key_verse: 2 Corinthians 12:9 - My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness.
2 Corinthians.description: 2 Corinthians is Paul most vulnerable letter, laying bare his apostolic trials, physical afflictions, and glorious calling as an ambassador of divine reconciliation.
2 Corinthians.review: 2 Corinthians proves that God power shines most brightly through fragile earthen vessels. When we are weak in ourselves, divine grace makes us triumphant and strong.

Galatians.name: Galatians
Galatians.author: Paul the Apostle
Galatians.theme: Freedom in Christ, Justification by Faith Alone, and the Fruit of the Spirit
Galatians.key_verse: Galatians 5:1 - Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free.
Galatians.description: Galatians defends the true Gospel against legalism, passionately proclaiming that salvation is through grace alone, not works of the law, empowering believers to walk by the Spirit.
Galatians.review: Galatians liberates the soul from the yoke of performance and legalistic fear. We are adopted sons and daughters called to bear love, joy, peace, and patience in freedom.

Ephesians.name: Ephesians
Ephesians.author: Paul the Apostle
Ephesians.theme: Spiritual Blessings, Grace through Faith, One New Humanity, and the Armor of God
Ephesians.key_verse: Ephesians 2:8-9 - For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God.
Ephesians.description: Ephesians unveils the cosmic scope of God plan, uniting Jews and Gentiles into one living temple and equipping believers with the full armor of God against spiritual darkness.
Ephesians.review: Ephesians grounds our identity as God cherished workmanship. We are seated with Christ in heavenly places, called to walk in unity, light, and courageous love.

Philippians.name: Philippians
Philippians.author: Paul the Apostle
Philippians.theme: Joy in the Lord, the Mind of Christ, Contentment, and Pressing On
Philippians.key_verse: Philippians 4:13 - I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
Philippians.description: Written from a Roman prison cell, Philippians radiates supernatural joy, urging believers to emulate the self-emptying humility of Christ and pursue the upward call of God.
Philippians.review: Philippians teaches that true joy is independent of outward circumstances. Through Christ who strengthens us, the peace of God guards our hearts in all contentment.

Colossians.name: Colossians
Colossians.author: Paul the Apostle
Colossians.theme: The Supremacy of Christ, Fullness in Him, and Putting on the New Self
Colossians.key_verse: Colossians 1:18 - That in all things he might have the preeminence.
Colossians.description: Colossians combats philosophical heresies by exalting Jesus as the preeminent Creator and Sustainer of the cosmos, in whom dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily.
Colossians.review: Colossians anchors our faith in the complete sufficiency of Jesus. We have been delivered from the domain of darkness into the kingdom of His beloved Son.

1 Thessalonians.name: 1 Thessalonians
1 Thessalonians.author: Paul the Apostle
1 Thessalonians.theme: Faith, Hope, Love, Sanctification, and the Blessed Return of the Lord
1 Thessalonians.key_verse: 1 Thessalonians 4:16-17 - For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout... so shall we ever be with the Lord.
1 Thessalonians.description: 1 Thessalonians commends an energetic young church for their work of faith and labor of love, providing holy encouragement concerning the sudden, glorious return of Jesus Christ.
1 Thessalonians.review: 1 Thessalonians comforts the grieving and motivates holy living in light of eternity. We live with our eyes on the horizon, eagerly awaiting the coming of our Lord.

2 Thessalonians.name: 2 Thessalonians
2 Thessalonians.author: Paul the Apostle
2 Thessalonians.theme: Perseverance in Persecution, the Man of Lawlessness, and Working Faithfully
2 Thessalonians.key_verse: 2 Thessalonians 3:3 - But the Lord is faithful, who shall stablish you, and keep you from evil.
2 Thessalonians.description: 2 Thessalonians clarifies misunderstandings about the day of the Lord, encouraging steadfast endurance amid fiery persecution and rebuking those who abandoned productive labor.
2 Thessalonians.review: 2 Thessalonians assures us that evil will not prevail. The Lord is faithful to guard our steps, defeat every adversary, and establish our hearts in every good word and work.

1 Timothy.name: 1 Timothy
1 Timothy.author: Paul the Apostle
1 Timothy.theme: Sound Doctrine, Church Leadership, Godliness with Contentment
1 Timothy.key_verse: 1 Timothy 6:6 - But godliness with contentment is great gain.
1 Timothy.description: Paul mentors young Timothy in pastoring the church at Ephesus, giving practical instructions on sound doctrine, qualifications for elders and deacons, and compassionate pastoral care.
1 Timothy.review: 1 Timothy equips believers to guard the sacred deposit of faith. Pursuing righteousness, godliness, faith, and patience yields great gain in this life and the next.

2 Timothy.name: 2 Timothy
2 Timothy.author: Paul the Apostle
2 Timothy.theme: Finishing the Race, the Power of Scripture, and Unashamed Faithfulness
2 Timothy.key_verse: 2 Timothy 4:7 - I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith.
2 Timothy.description: Writing from a cold dungeon facing imminent martyrdom, Paul pens his poignant final testament, charging Timothy to preach the word in season and out, and finish his race with courage.
2 Timothy.review: 2 Timothy inspires uncompromising perseverance to the very end. Rooted in God inspired Word, we do not receive a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and a sound mind.

Titus.name: Titus
Titus.author: Paul the Apostle
Titus.theme: Appointing Elders, Sound Teaching, and Devotion to Good Works
Titus.key_verse: Titus 2:11 - For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men.
Titus.description: Titus provides pastoral counsel for establishing healthy order in the unruly churches of Crete, emphasizing that sound biblical doctrine must bear fruit in upright, attractive living.
Titus.review: Titus shows that saving grace transforms everyday conduct. Those who trust in God are purified and made zealous for good works that bless society and honor our Savior.

Philemon.name: Philemon
Philemon.author: Paul the Apostle
Philemon.theme: Reconciliation, Forgiveness, and Receiving a Brother in Christ
Philemon.key_verse: Philemon 1:16 - Not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved.
Philemon.description: Philemon is a masterclass in tactful Christian reconciliation, pleading on behalf of Onesimus, a runaway slave, that he be welcomed back not as property, but as a beloved brother.
Philemon.review: Philemon illustrates the transformative power of forgiveness and Christian equality. In the family of God, earthly barriers dissolve and reconciliation reigns supreme.

Hebrews.name: Hebrews
Hebrews.author: Unknown (Paul, Apollos, or Barnabas)
Hebrews.theme: The Supremacy of Christ over Angels, Moses, and the Priesthood; Enduring Faith
Hebrews.key_verse: Hebrews 11:1 - Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
Hebrews.description: Hebrews demonstrates that Jesus Christ is superior to angels, Moses, and the levitical priesthood, mediating a better covenant built on eternal promises and urging believers to hold fast.
Hebrews.review: Hebrews urges us to run the race with endurance, fixing our eyes upon Jesus, the author and finisher of our faith. He is the same yesterday, today, and forever.

James.name: James
James.author: James the Brother of Jesus
James.theme: Faith without Works is Dead, Taming the Tongue, and Heavenly Wisdom
James.key_verse: James 1:22 - But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
James.description: James offers direct, practical wisdom on enduring trials with joy, controlling the tongue, caring for orphans and widows, and proving living faith through active deeds of compassion.
James.review: James reminds us that genuine faith is intensely practical. Faith without deeds of love is dead, but humble wisdom from above is peaceable, gentle, and full of good fruits.

1 Peter.name: 1 Peter
1 Peter.author: Peter the Apostle
1 Peter.theme: Living Hope, Joy amidst Persecution, and Standing Firm in Grace
1 Peter.key_verse: 1 Peter 1:3 - Begotten us again unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead.
1 Peter.description: Peter comforts believers scattered throughout the Roman empire facing hostility, pointing them to their imperishable heavenly inheritance and calling them to live as a royal priesthood.
1 Peter.review: 1 Peter fortifies the believer soul against suffering. After we have suffered a little while, the God of all grace will Himself restore, confirm, strengthen, and establish us.

2 Peter.name: 2 Peter
2 Peter.author: Peter the Apostle
2 Peter.theme: Growing in Grace, False Teachers, and the Day of the Lord
2 Peter.key_verse: 2 Peter 3:18 - But grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.
2 Peter.description: In his farewell warning, Peter urges believers to add virtues to their faith, exposes dangerous deceptive teachers, and affirms that the delayed day of the Lord reflects divine patience.
2 Peter.review: 2 Peter charges us to cultivate steady spiritual maturity. We look forward with holy expectancy to a new heaven and a new earth where righteousness dwells forever.

1 John.name: 1 John
1 John.author: John the Apostle
1 John.theme: Walking in Light, Love for the Brethren, and Assurance of Eternal Life
1 John.key_verse: 1 John 4:19 - We love him, because he first loved us.
1 John.description: 1 John provides tests of genuine spiritual fellowship: walking in the light, obeying divine commandments, practicing genuine love for brothers and sisters, and abiding in truth.
1 John.review: 1 John pours comforting assurance into our hearts. God is love, and whoever abides in love abides in God; perfect love casts out all fear and grants boldness in His presence.

2 John.name: 2 John
2 John.author: John the Apostle
2 John.theme: Walking in Truth and Love, Guarding against Deceivers
2 John.key_verse: 2 John 1:6 - And this is love, that we walk after his commandments.
2 John.description: Writing to an elect lady and her children, John rejoices to see believers walking in the truth, insisting that Christian love and adherence to apostolic truth are inseparable.
2 John.review: 2 John highlights the vital harmony between truth and love. We must love passionately while remaining vigilant against deceptive compromises that would erode our faith.

3 John.name: 3 John
3 John.author: John the Apostle
3 John.theme: Hospitality to Truth, Supporting Fellow Laborers, and Rejecting Pride
3 John.key_verse: 3 John 1:4 - I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth.
3 John.description: 3 John commends Gaius for his generous hospitality to traveling missionaries while confronting the arrogant Diotrephes who refused fellowship and loved to put himself first.
3 John.review: 3 John affirms that supporting those who proclaim truth makes us fellow laborers in the Gospel. Selfless generosity and humble service bring supreme joy to God family.

Jude.name: Jude
Jude.author: Jude the Brother of Jesus and James
Jude.theme: Contending for the Faith, Warning against Apostasy, and Kept in Love
Jude.key_verse: Jude 1:24-25 - Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy.
Jude.description: Jude urges believers to contend earnestly for the faith once delivered to the saints, exposing false teachers and concluding with one of the most magnificent doxologies in all Scripture.
Jude.review: Jude assures us that while storms of deception rage, our Savior is able to keep us from stumbling and present us blameless before His presence with exceeding joy.

Revelation.name: Revelation
Revelation.author: John the Beloved Apostle
Revelation.theme: The Glorified Christ, Victory over the Dragon, and the New Jerusalem
Revelation.key_verse: Revelation 21:4 - And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death.
Revelation.description: Revelation unveils the ultimate triumph of the Lamb who was slain, pulling back the veil of earthly history to reveal cosmic judgment, the fall of Babylon, and the descent of the New Jerusalem.
Revelation.review: Revelation delivers supreme consolation: Jesus reigns as King of kings and Lord of lords! Every tear shall be wiped away, all things made new, and God shall dwell with His people forever.
